title: Project Overview and Rules
description: README.md is the declared source of truth for architecture, routes, tables and environment variables, and CLAUDE.md sets the working conventions (branch-per-task, plans, navigation rules). Read these first to get the vocabulary of NovelHub, a light novel, manga and Fandom reading platform split into a Next.js frontend, a catalog service and several satellite services.

title: Docker Compose and Gateway
description: docker-compose.yml wires every service together, and nginx.conf is the gateway that routes browser traffic to the frontend and to each backend service. Understanding this topology explains why the catalog is still reachable as 'backend' inside the Docker network and how requests are fanned out.
languageLesson: docker-compose describes a multi-container system declaratively; service names double as DNS names on the internal network, and mounted config files such as nginx.conf need an explicit reload.

title: Microservice Split Plan
description: Plan/microservices.md has the highest fan-in among the documents and records how functionality was carved out of the original catalog monolith into identity, library, workspace, messaging, media, community and recommender services. Use it as the map for the service steps that follow.

title: Catalog Service Core
description: The catalog service is the main Express backend. server.ts is its HTTP entry point and worker.ts runs background jobs, while config/db.ts, env.ts and the logger are the shared foundations used by most of its files.
languageLesson: Express 4 does not catch errors thrown in async handlers, so handlers need try/catch or .catch(next), as CLAUDE.md warns.

title: Auth and Signed Identity Headers
description: auth.middleware.ts is imported widely across catalog and verifies the signed X-User-* headers that the gateway and identity service attach. Each service trusts only headers signed with its own key, which is the central security pattern joining the services.

title: Frontend Foundations
description: The Next.js frontend builds on a few shared pieces: AuthContext for session state, session.ts and apiJson.ts for API calls that carry the CSRF header, and nav-aware Link and BackLink components that implement the back-navigation rules from CLAUDE.md.
languageLesson: React context shares state such as the signed-in user with the whole tree, without passing props through every level.

title: Go Services
description: Identity, library, workspace and messaging are small Go services, each with its own main.go and its own database migrations. They show the pattern of one service owning one database and exposing a narrow API behind the gateway.
languageLesson: Go builds each service into one static binary, which is why the Dockerfiles use a multi-stage build ending in a scratch image.

title: Media, Community and Recommender
description: The media service (Node, exports and images), the community service (Node) and the recommender (Python, started via rec/__main__.py) cover the specialised workloads. Each has its own Dockerfile and, where it stores data, its own migrations, so it can be built and scaled on its own.

title: Database Schema and Migrations
description: sql/database.sql is the catalog schema and sql/migrations adds idempotent numbered changes that must be copied into it, while catalog/prisma/schema.prisma describes the same data for Prisma. Per-service migrations such as identity's 001_init.sql sit next to each service.
languageLesson: Idempotent SQL migrations (IF NOT EXISTS, guarded ALTERs) can be re-run safely, which suits the project's migrate script.

title: Event Contracts
description: The events folder holds versioned JSON schemas, all built around envelope.v1.json, for events like story viewed, bookmark created and revision merged. Services publish and consume these to stay decoupled; the catalog's queue.service.ts is the producer side in catalog.

title: Navigation and Performance Plans
description: Plan/navigation.md and Plan/load.md capture frontend design decisions: no breadcrumbs, a per-tab page stack, and hover-triggered prefetching through the shared Link. Reading them explains the odd restrictions on router.back and next/link.
